title: Sowing and planting A sound start

references.role: Timber staging and John sowing in a module tray.
Crop of hands, cuff, slats and tray from the same camera frame.
Independent April angle with seed trays and navy sleeve.

adaptation: The outer pictures stage direct sowing and final planting in deep growing containers on the greenhouse bench. The middle picture shows a labelled module tray.
prompt:
Create ONE wide 3:1 photographic triptych for an English vegetable-growing book. Three different tightly composed, equal, SQUARE photographs, in ONE horizontal row, each taking exactly one third. Edge to edge with straight hard cuts at the thirds. No text overlays, borders, margins or graphics. Use the first three attached ACTUAL photographs of John Lennon's small Cornish greenhouse as material and lighting reference: the weathered, narrow brown slats with visible spaces, aluminium glazing bars, blue shed outside the glass and mature gardener's hands. Last attached drawing gives ONLY the three page actions. Do not imitate illustrations. These must look like genuine close photographs of hands midway through practical jobs in the same greenhouse, taken for Hackriculture, not generic studio stock. Close enough to teach each job in a 48 mm square. Tight three-quarter overhead macro/normal perspective; hands and work fill the frame, small glimpses of worn slats around the work, at most a hint of soft glass behind. Do not show John's head, torso or face. Real pores, worn fingernails and a trace of soil, natural mature light British skin matching attached hands, functional gestures; hands enter anatomically from the camera-side edge or side, no duplicated digits. Restrained natural colour, UK diffuse greenhouse daylight, moderate depth of field, sharp on point of action.

LEFT — Direct sowing. A deep, practical final-growing planter of fine, dark damp soil, resting on John's slatted greenhouse workbench. Camera close: only a corner of rim and wood visible, bulk of frame is the surface. John's bare thumb and forefinger just releasing a few tiny buff, elongated carrot seeds spaced thinly into a SINGLE continuous shallow straight seed drill; unambiguously a slender groove in fine natural soil, just a few millimetres deep, crumbly sloping sides. A few real-size seeds already in the groove catch light subtly. Main action large and readable; avoid enormous seeds, a trench or root vegetables. Same flecked oatmeal jumper cuff as the footage.
CENTRE — Start under cover. Change the angle a little while keeping that same bench. A black plastic module tray, recognisable square individual cells with clearly visible cell edges and compost, a small young lettuce seedling in each of several cells. Small two-to-three leaf nursery plants in soft muted greens, naturally varied. John's hand slipping one slender off-white reusable plant label with a little unobtrusive authentic pencil handwriting 'Little Gem' and '12/3' into compost just inside the corner of a cell, other hand lightly steadying the tray rim. Label and living tray are subordinate to the work, no headings. Oatmeal cuff. Do not mix seed sowing with lifting or planting on this panel.
RIGHT — Plant them out. A few weeks later: a navy sweater cuff such as in April footage. A close view over a deep bench-top final-growing container with open growing space, emphatically not another cell tray. John's bare fingertips cradle the sides of ONE intact small lettuce plug (four tender true leaves, dark cohesive plug showing a few very fine pale roots) as he lowers it straight into a matching planting hole in damp crumbly soil. Catch it halfway in, bottom tucked into hole, part of root ball still above, aligned for crown at the surface. No pulling leaves or gripping stems. Spare hand can steady soil beside hole if natural. Optional glimpse of small worn metal trowel off to the side if it adds scale. Real restrained light, no giant mature lettuce. Compose so hole, rootball, hand and seedling read as one action.

The three images must each remain complete and useful when split. Keep main hands, action and essential planting details well away from the outermost 5% and from joins. Deep containers for the outer pictures allow direct-sowing and final planting on a real workbench. No soil sitting loose in a heap on the timber. No visual diagram, display of tools or floating objects.
label_correction_prompt:
Retouch this exact picture for the printed book. It is one wide strip of three square real-looking close photographs. Make one tiny local edit only, to the ink on the white plant marker in the central photo. Remove every existing grey squiggle, keep the same white plastic marker in the same hand/compost position, and write the following clearly and literally. Turn the writing across the face into short, easily read horizontal lines, one word or date per line:
Little
Gem
12/3
Nothing else printed or written on the label. 'Little' has six letters. 'Gem' has three letters. '12/3' is the sowing date, four characters. A practical gardener’s legible fine black handwritten lettering, evenly spaced, distinctly readable, with all lines fitting within the visible label below John's fingers and above the soil line. Let the label be a fraction wider if needed. Keep everything else visually identical to this reference: exact composition, colours, three equal square photographic panels, wooden staging, hands, seed drill with tiny carrot seeds at left, lettuce plugs in black tray at centre and the plug being set in compost at right. No heading, writing or graphics anywhere else. Do not resize the jobs, move the panel boundaries, expand the scenery or add panels. Final image 3:1 panoramic triptych.
